title: Orgrimmar
body: Orgrimmar is the capital of the Horde, carved into a canyon of red stone in the mountains of northern Durotar. Thrall raised it after the battle at Mount Hyjal with the help of goblins, tauren and the Darkspear, and named it for Orgrim Doomhammer, the mentor who passed the Horde into his hands. Its valleys are joined by tunnels and ramps, from the Valley of Strength behind the gate to the Valley of Wisdom, where the Warchief holds court.

parts.body: In recent years the blood elves of Silvermoon, championed by the Forsaken, have joined the Horde, and their ambassador now speaks for Quel'Thalas in Grommash Hold.
When traitors seized the Undercity after the Wrathgate, Orgrimmar shut its shops by order of the Warchief, took in the Forsaken who fled, and lived under martial law.

title: Valley of Strength
body: Past the great gate lies the Valley of Strength, with its bank, auction house, wind rider tower and the Broken Tusk inn, where fighters lay their axes by the fire. Overlord Runthak keeps order here and carries out the Warchief's commands without question, and before the gathered city he cries the Horde's great victories and mounts the head of a fallen foe for all to see.

parts.body: The duty was not always his: High Overlord Saurfang once proclaimed the Horde's triumphs here, but Saurfang has gone north to Warsong Hold in Northrend.

title: Valley of Wisdom
body: The Valley of Wisdom is the high seat of the city, where shaman of orc, troll and tauren blood teach and the far seer Zor Lonetree sends young heroes wherever they are needed. Here stands Grommash Hold, the Warchief's fortress, named for Grom Hellscream, whose blow slew Mannoroth and freed the orcs from the demon's curse; the demon's armor stands outside, so the Horde will remember how hard it fought to regain its honor.

parts.body: Since the blood elves joined the Horde, Ambassador Dawnsinger of Silvermoon has kept a place in the hold, sending heroes to the Horde's outposts to cement the bond.

title: Cleft of Shadow
body: Off the Drag a crevasse splits the rock of Orgrimmar, open only to a strip of sky, and the city's less savory folk live in its gloom. Warlocks of the Horde train here, among them Neeru Fireblade, who proclaims his loyalty to the Warchief, and rogues teach stealth and poison. At its bottom opens Ragefire Chasm, the burning caverns beneath the city, where a demon cult works in secret.

title: Valley of Honor
body: The Valley of Honor, in the northeast of the city, is Orgrimmar's martial quarter, where warriors and hunters train, smiths work the forges and battlemasters send fighters to the fields of war. Not everything here is war: an orphanage shelters children who lost their parents to the Horde's many conflicts, a quiet reminder of the price of all that glory.

parts.body: Of late the valley's old arena has opened its floor as the Ring of Valor, where fighters meet among platforms that rise and sink around them.

title: Valley of Spirits
body: The Valley of Spirits, a long and narrow valley in the southwest of the city, is the quarter of the Darkspear trolls. Their huts and lodges crowd its slopes, troll mages teach in Darkbriar Lodge, and the troll priests greet strangers with a warning to respect their ways, or have a curse laid on them and theirs.

parts.body: A portal now shimmers on the upper floor of Darkbriar Lodge, opening across the sea onto the Blasted Lands near the Dark Portal, for travelers bound for Outland.

title: Vol'jin
body: Vol'jin, son of Sen'jin, leads the Darkspear trolls. When Thrall's orcs freed his people from their captors on a storm swept isle, where his father was slain, Vol'jin pledged the tribe to the Horde and followed the orcs to Kalimdor. Now he stands in the Warchief's chamber as an adviser. He has no love for humans, and he has never hidden his doubts about Thrall's dealings with them.

parts.body: When Admiral Proudmoore's sealed orders reached Orgrimmar, Vol'jin reminded all who would hear that he had urged Thrall countless times not to trust the humans.

title: Eitrigg
body: Eitrigg is an old warrior of the Blackrock clan, a veteran of the First and Second Wars. His sons died at Blackrock Spire in Rend Blackhand's war with the Dark Irons, and refusing to serve such a fool he lived as a hermit near Hearthglen, until humans captured him. Tirion Fordring and Thrall saved him from execution, and the Warchief made him an adviser in his throne room.

parts.body: In time Tirion, now Highlord of the Argent Crusade, asked the Warchief for a good orc at his side, and Eitrigg went north to serve the Crusade at the Argent Stand in Zul'Drak.
